notes: US 708: the paper explicitly equates it with HVS2 at T:p2-b2; T:p2-b5 cites Hirsch et al. (2005) and explicitly states unboundness, so it is recorded as follow_up. HVS 1: the HVS 1/HVS1 forms are treated as one designation; T:p1-b9 calls it the prototype, and T:p3-b3 lists it among the reanalyzed HVS. HVS 4: T:p3-b3 lists it among the HVS with new MMT spectra, and T:p3-b2 attributes the survey discoveries to Brown et al.; follow_up. HVS 5: same evidence as HVS 4 (T:p3-b2, T:p3-b3). HVS 6: same evidence as HVS 4 (T:p3-b2, T:p3-b3). HVS 7: same evidence as HVS 4 (T:p3-b2, T:p3-b3). HE 0437−5439: T:p5-b2 identifies it as the third HVS from Edelmann et al. (2005); the preferred LMC origin at T:p6-b1 does not change its follow_up status. The paper does not explicitly print an HVS-number alias, so none is added. HD 271791: T:p2-b3 calls the Section 5 object a candidate HVS and T:p8-b2 retains it as a newly discovered candidate; T:p6-b5 gives a proper-motion-dependent rest-frame velocity range, so no unique boundness value is asserted. Survey group: for HVS 4, HVS 5, HVS 6, and HVS 7, only these individually designated members of the paper's seven-new-HVS discussion (T:p1-b11) are identifiable; no unnamed group members are expanded.

US 708: The paper states that US 708 is unbound to the Galaxy (T:p2-b5) but reports no numerical bound or unbound probability, so no probability quantity is recorded. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or proper motion values are reported for US 708 (proper motions are noted only as future tests, T:p2-b6). No Galactocentric radius is reported.

HVS 1: HVS 1 is discussed in T:p3-b5 and shown in Figure 2 (I:p4-b0, I:p4-b1), but the supplied material reports no eligible positional or kinematic quantity for it. The only explicit numerical property is v sin i = 190 km/s, which is not among the requested quantities.

HVS 4: HVS 4 is mentioned only as one of the stars whose MMT spectra were analyzed and as a point in the (T_eff, log g) diagrams (Fig. 2, I:p4-b0 and I:p4-b1). The paper does not report right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS 4, so no requested quantity can be extracted.

HVS 5: HVS 5 is only mentioned as one of the late B-type HVSs whose MMT spectra were analyzed and plotted in the (T_eff, log g) diagrams (Fig. 2, I:p4-b0 and I:p4-b1); the paper reports no individual values for HVS 5 for any of the target quantities (RA, Dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability). Its atmospheric parameters (T_eff, log g) shown in Fig. 2 are not among the quantities to be extracted.

HVS 6: HVS 6 is discussed only as having evidence for rotational broadening (T:p3-b5; T:p8-b2) and as a point in the Teff–log g diagrams (I:p4-b0; I:p4-b1). The paper does not report values for any requested quantity (position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for HVS 6.

HVS 7: HVS 7 is discussed in the text and plotted in the (T_eff, log g) diagrams (T:p3-b3, T:p3-b5, T:p4-b1; I:p4-b0, I:p4-b1), but the paper reports no numeric values for any of the requested quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper-motion components, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability). Its reported subsolar helium abundance and diagram position are not among the requested quantities, so no values are extracted.

HE 0437−5439: At T:p5-b2 and T:p5-b5 the paper gives alternative model-dependent distances for HE 0437−5439. At T:p5-b5 the proper-motion values are explicitly "required" values for the speculative 0.5 Msun scenario, not catalog measurements. The 927 km/s mentioned at T:p5-b5 is an ejection speed in that scenario, not a heliocentric radial velocity or a present-day Galactic-rest-frame speed, so it was not extracted. The 18 kpc mentioned at T:p5-b3 is not a heliocentric distance. No right ascension, declination, parallax, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HE 0437−5439.
